scenarios.title: Bullish Impulse & Continuation
scenarios.question: What market structure is developing as price breaches 1.0880 and establishes a higher floor at 1.0865?
scenarios.explanation: Price forms consecutive Higher Highs (1.0880 -> 1.0910 -> 1.0935) and Higher Lows (1.0840 -> 1.0865), confirming bullish trend continuation.

scenarios.title: Stair-Step Trend Expansion
scenarios.question: Prior resistance at 150.50 was broken and held as a new higher low. What structure is demonstrated?
scenarios.explanation: In a healthy stair-step uptrend, prior swing highs are broken and then retested as support floors, creating durable Higher Lows.

scenarios.title: Deep Pullback Bullish Defense
scenarios.question: Price made a steep retracement to 1.2600 before bouncing and breaking 1.2660. Is the uptrend intact?

options.text: Yes, 1.2600 held above prior low (Valid HL)
No, deep pullbacks always invalidate trends
No, this is a confirmed downtrend

scenarios.explanation: As long as price forms a Higher Low above the origin low (1.2545) and exceeds the prior swing high (1.2660), the uptrend structure remains valid.

scenarios.title: Trend Acceleration Wave
scenarios.question: Pullback sizes are shrinking while upward thrusts are expanding. What does this indicate?

options.text: Bullish Trend Acceleration & Strong Buyer Dominance

scenarios.explanation: When impulse waves grow larger and corrective pullbacks become shallower, momentum is accelerating in the direction of the dominant uptrend.

scenarios.title: Standard Lower High & Lower Low Cascade
scenarios.question: What market structure is established by this succession of lower peaks and deeper valleys?
scenarios.explanation: Sellers consistently step in at lower price points (LH) and push price below prior lows (LL), confirming a bearish trend.

scenarios.title: Breakdown Retest Rejection
scenarios.question: Price broke 1.2700 support, rallied to test 1.2700 from below, printed a long upper wick, and dropped. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Old support at 1.2700 flipped to new resistance. The failed retest confirms seller dominance and continues the downtrend.

scenarios.title: Descending Channel Cascade
scenarios.question: Price is cycling between parallel downward-sloping boundary lines. What structure is this?
scenarios.explanation: A descending channel forms when both swing highs and swing lows can be connected by parallel downward-sloping trendlines.

scenarios.title: Failed Rally Exhaustion
scenarios.question: After each sharp selloff, relief rallies are weak and immediately rejected below previous peaks. What does this confirm?
scenarios.explanation: When buyers lack the volume to mount substantial counter-trend pullbacks, sellers remain firmly in control.

scenarios.title: Clean Horizontal Range Box
scenarios.question: Price oscillates between 1.0810 and 1.0890 without making Higher Highs or Lower Lows. What is this market state?
scenarios.explanation: Equal highs at 1.0890 and equal lows at 1.0810 define a balanced range where neither buyers nor sellers have directional control.

scenarios.title: Volatility Compression inside Range
scenarios.question: Candle ranges and swing amplitudes are narrowing into a symmetrical squeeze. What structure is this?
scenarios.explanation: Volatility compression occurs when market participants await new information, contracting price toward equilibrium before an impending expansion.

scenarios.title: Wide Choppy Range with Midpoint Rejections
scenarios.question: Price respects both outer extremes (1.2600 & 1.2700) and hesitates at the 50% midpoint (1.2650). What does this represent?

options.text: Balanced Range Structure with Active Equilibrium (Mid-Range)

scenarios.explanation: Ranges often feature a prominent 50% equilibrium level where price hesitates between rotational moves across the boundary extremes.

scenarios.title: Range Expansion Squeeze
scenarios.question: Before breaking out at 2040, price printed ascending lows against the flat ceiling. What was this?

options.text: Ascending Pressure Build-Up (Higher Lows into Resistance)

scenarios.explanation: Rising swing lows against a flat resistance level show aggressive buyer absorption, frequently preceding an upward range expansion.

scenarios.title: Major Horizontal Demand Floor Defense
scenarios.question: Price reached 1.0800, printed long lower wicks, and surged with strong green bodies. What level reaction occurred?
scenarios.explanation: Rejection wicks and strong follow-through buying confirm that institutional demand is actively defending the 1.0800 price floor.

scenarios.title: Dynamic Demand Zone Cushion
scenarios.question: Price dipped through 150.20 down to 150.02 within the broad zone before rapidly closing back upward. How should this level be treated?

options.text: As a Support Zone (Price Area rather than a single fixed tick)

scenarios.explanation: Key market levels are zones of interest rather than hairline coordinates; small penetrations that quickly reject reinforce the zone's validity.

scenarios.title: Triple Support Floor Test
scenarios.question: 1.2500 was tested three separate times, each resulting in immediate buying. What does this confirm?
scenarios.explanation: Multiple successful tests of a major horizontal price point confirm significant liquidity and buyer conviction at support.

scenarios.title: Prior Swing Low Demand Defense
scenarios.question: When price returned to the historical swing low of 2020, buyers stepped in aggressively. What is this?

options.text: Prior Swing Low Acting as Support Memory

scenarios.explanation: Prior swing lows represent established price floors where institutional buyers historically found value.

scenarios.title: Heavy Supply Ceiling Rejection
scenarios.question: Price repeatedly struck 1.2800, printed long upper wicks, and collapsed into lower territory. What happened?
scenarios.explanation: Multiple upper wick rejections at the 1.2800 ceiling followed by large bearish bodies confirm seller defense at resistance.

scenarios.title: Prior Swing High Resistance Barrier
scenarios.question: When price returned to the previous swing high of 2065, sellers capped the rally and forced a sharp decline. What principle is shown?

options.text: Prior Swing High Acting as Resistance Memory

scenarios.explanation: Previous major swing highs represent historical price memory where sellers previously overwhelmed buyers, establishing clear horizontal resistance.

scenarios.title: Dynamic Supply Zone Ceiling
scenarios.question: Price entered the 1.0915-1.0935 zone, printed upper rejection wicks, and collapsed into lower support. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Supply zones represent areas of heavy pending sell orders that halt upward momentum and reverse price downward.

scenarios.title: Repeated Resistance Weakening vs. Hold
scenarios.question: Rejections from 152.00 became progressively shallower before price broke out. What caused this?
scenarios.explanation: Each time resistance is tested with shallower pullbacks, available sell orders are absorbed, weakening the level until a breakout occurs.

scenarios.title: Confirmed Resistance Breakout with Full Body Close
scenarios.question: Candle 4 closed firmly at 1.0890 (well above 1.0850) and Candle 5 expanded to 1.0920. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: A confirmed breakout requires a full candle body closing outside the boundary accompanied by immediate directional follow-through.

scenarios.title: Confirmed Support Breakdown Cascade
scenarios.question: Price closed heavily beneath the 150.00 floor at 149.35 with expanding red volume. What structure event occurred?
scenarios.explanation: When price decisively closes below a structural support floor and continues dropping, the level is officially broken.

scenarios.title: Breakout Without Follow-Through (Stall)
scenarios.question: Price closed above 1.2750 but stalled for two candles before surging higher. What caution is required during stalls?

options.text: Wait for Confirmed Follow-Through rather than chasing initial stalls
Immediately short because every stall is a fakeout

scenarios.explanation: Breakouts occasionally experience brief volume stalls before expansion; waiting for follow-through avoids getting trapped in indecision.

scenarios.title: High-Volume Momentum Breakout
scenarios.question: A large Marubozu green candle smashed through 2050 with no upper wick and closed at 2070. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: A large full-bodied candle closing far outside the broken level with minimal wicks signifies institutional momentum breakout.

scenarios.title: Classic Bull Trap (Liquidity Wick Above Resistance)
scenarios.question: Candle 3 spiked to 1.2835 (above 1.2800) but closed at 1.2792 inside the range, followed by a sharp drop. What was this?

options.text: Bullish Fakeout / Bull Trap (Wick Spike & Failure)

scenarios.explanation: A wick piercing resistance that closes back inside the range is a liquidity sweep/fakeout, trapping breakout buyers before reversing downward.

scenarios.title: Bear Trap (Wick Sweep Below Support)
scenarios.question: Price spiked down to 2018 beneath 2030 support, instantly closed at 2032, and rocketed upward. What is this?

options.text: Bear Trap / Liquidity Sweep below Support

scenarios.explanation: Price briefly ran stop-losses below support before institutional demand absorbed the orders and drove price aggressively higher.

scenarios.title: Two-Candle False Breakout (Immediate Reversal)
scenarios.question: Candle 2 closed above 1.0900, but Candle 3 immediately completely engulfed it and closed far below. What occurred?
scenarios.explanation: A breakout candle immediately negated by an opposing engulfing candle is a trap, indicating aggressive institutional distribution.

scenarios.title: Repeated Failed Breakouts (Range Top Exhaustion)
scenarios.question: Price repeatedly spiked above 151.00 but closed lower every time, culminating in a breakdown. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Multiple failed attempts to hold above resistance signal buyer exhaustion and lead to aggressive downside resolution.

scenarios.title: Breakout + Flawless Retest Confirmation
scenarios.question: After breaking 1.0900, price pulled back gently to touch 1.0900 from above and printed a strong green candle. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: When broken resistance holds as newly established support on a retest, it provides structural confirmation of trend continuation.

scenarios.title: Failed Retest with Return to Range
scenarios.question: Price broke 151.00, attempted to hold, but failed and slipped back into the prior range with heavy selling. What occurred?

options.text: Failed Retest & Return to Range (Breakout Failure)

scenarios.explanation: If price fails to hold above the breakout level on the retest and drops back into the previous range, the breakout has failed.

scenarios.title: Breakdown + Bearish Retest Rejection
scenarios.question: Price broke below 1.2600, rallied to touch 1.2600 from beneath, and immediately printed a long upper wick and fell. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: A broken support level retested from beneath and rejected confirms that sellers now control that price zone.

scenarios.title: Shallow Retest Continuation
scenarios.question: The pullback was so shallow that price did not even touch the broken 2040 level before rocketing higher. What does this reveal?

options.text: Extremely Strong Buyer Demand (Shallow Front-Run Retest)

scenarios.explanation: When demand is exceptionally strong, buyers step in before price can touch the exact retest level, creating shallow continuation.

scenarios.title: Break of Structure (BOS) from Uptrend to Downtrend
scenarios.question: After making a Lower High, price broke decisively beneath the previous Higher Low of 1.0850. What happened?
scenarios.explanation: When price fails to make a new high and subsequently breaks below the prior Higher Low, market structure shifts from bullish to bearish.

scenarios.title: Change of Character (CHoCH) Bottom Shift
scenarios.question: In a downtrend, price formed a Higher Low and then breached the last Lower High at 1.2650. What is this structural event?

options.text: Change of Character (CHoCH) / Bullish Reversal Shift

scenarios.explanation: A Change of Character occurs when price establishes its first higher low and breaks above the most recent lower high in a downtrend.

scenarios.title: Trend to Range Structural Stall
scenarios.question: Price halted Higher High progression and began bouncing between 150.20 and 151.50. What structural shift occurred?
scenarios.explanation: When price stops making higher extremes and oscillates between established boundaries, the market has transitioned from a trending regime to a range.

scenarios.title: Failed Swing Low Shift
scenarios.question: Sellers failed to make a new Lower Low, printing a Higher Low at 2035 followed by a break of 2048. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: A failure swing occurs when sellers cannot push price past the previous low, signaling that buyer pressure has overpowered seller momentum.

scenarios.title: Equal Highs Liquidity Pool Sweep
scenarios.question: Triple equal peaks formed at 151.50 before a single candle spiked to 151.85 and collapsed. What occurred?
scenarios.explanation: Equal highs attract large clusters of stop-loss buy orders. Smart money triggers these stops to obtain sell liquidity before driving price down.

scenarios.title: Equal Lows Liquidity Pool Sweep
scenarios.question: Triple equal bottoms at 1.0800 were swept down to 1.0765 before an explosive rally. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Equal lows create obvious stop-loss levels. Sweeping below these points engineers sell liquidity to fill large institutional buy orders.

scenarios.title: Breakout After Equal Highs Accumulation
scenarios.question: After touching equal highs at 1.2800 twice with rising lows, price closed firmly at 1.2850. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Unlike a fakeout, this scenario showed full body candle close above the equal highs with expanding follow-through volume.

scenarios.title: Ascending Channel Boundary Bounce
scenarios.question: Price bounces reliably each time it meets the upward-sloping lower trendline. What structure is demonstrated?
scenarios.explanation: An ascending channel creates an upward sloping price corridor where the lower line provides dynamic support and the upper line provides dynamic resistance.

scenarios.title: Descending Channel Resistance Touch
scenarios.question: Price repeatedly touches and rejects from the descending diagonal upper ceiling. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: The downward sloping upper line of a descending channel acts as dynamic resistance, offering high-probability continuation zones.

scenarios.title: Channel Breakdown Acceleration
scenarios.question: Price broke decisively below the ascending channel's support trendline with an oversized red candle. What occurred?
scenarios.explanation: When price breaches the lower boundary of an ascending channel, upward momentum is broken and a trend transition or reversal begins.

scenarios.title: Failed Channel Breakout (Return to Channel)
scenarios.question: Price pierced the upper boundary of the channel with a long wick but closed back inside and reversed to the lower line. What was this?
scenarios.explanation: Spiking beyond channel boundaries and closing back inside traps premature breakout traders and often triggers a fast rotation to the opposite boundary.

scenarios.title: Multi-Factor Confluence (Horizontal Support + Trendline)
scenarios.question: At 2040, horizontal prior resistance and an ascending trendline intersect, producing a powerful bounce. What is this?
scenarios.explanation: Confluence occurs when two or more independent technical factors (e.g. prior resistance turned support + upward trendline) align at the exact same price zone.

scenarios.title: Confluence Resistance (Prior Swing High + Round Number)
scenarios.question: 1.3000 aligns a major psychological round number with a previous multi-month swing high. What is this zone called?
scenarios.explanation: Major psychological round numbers that overlap with historical swing highs create powerful multi-factor confluence.

scenarios.title: Triple Confluence (Support Flip + Trendline + Demand Zone)
scenarios.question: 150.00 represents a broken resistance flip, an ascending trendline contact, and an institutional round number. What type of setup is this?
scenarios.explanation: When three independent structural elements converge at one level, the probability of price respecting the zone increases dramatically.

scenarios.title: Horizontal Support Hold
scenarios.question: Price repeatedly halted at 1.0800 and bounced upward. What does 1.0800 represent?
scenarios.explanation: 1.0800 acted as a horizontal support floor where buyer demand defended price multiple times.

scenarios.title: Double Bottom Support Defense
scenarios.question: What structural formation is formed by the twin troughs at 150.00?
scenarios.explanation: Two distinct troughs holding at the same horizontal price level (150.00) form a Double Bottom at support.

scenarios.title: Triple Support Test Shelf
scenarios.question: What occurred at the 1.2500 level across the 6-candle sequence?
scenarios.explanation: 1.2500 was tested three separate times without breaking, establishing a robust support shelf.

scenarios.title: Strong Pin / Hammer Rejection at Support
scenarios.question: How did buyers respond when price probed below 2000.0 in candle #2?
scenarios.explanation: The long lower tail down to 1998 and close back at 2014 demonstrated aggressive buying defense at support.

scenarios.title: Support Demand Zone
scenarios.question: Instead of a single line, price turned within 1.0700–1.0720. What is this concept?
scenarios.explanation: Institutions often accumulate across a price area rather than a single tick, creating a Support Zone.

scenarios.title: Weak Support Reaction (Grinding Floor)
scenarios.question: What did the shallow, sluggish bounces at 0.8500 indicate before the breakdown?
scenarios.explanation: Failing to bounce with strength away from support indicates diminishing buyer demand, making a breakdown more likely.

scenarios.title: Prior Swing Low Acting as Support
scenarios.question: What structural reference provided support for candle #4?
scenarios.explanation: Prior market swing lows frequently act as horizontal support when revisited by price.

scenarios.title: Higher Low Structural Support
scenarios.question: What role did the 1.0840 price level serve in candle #2?

options.text: Higher Low Support within an Uptrend

scenarios.explanation: 1.0840 served as the structural Higher Low support floor defending the prevailing uptrend.

scenarios.title: Range Box Support Boundary
scenarios.question: What is 100.0 in this horizontal consolidation box?
scenarios.explanation: 100.0 marks the lower boundary (support floor) of the horizontal range.

scenarios.title: Rising Support Pressure
scenarios.question: What did the sequence of higher lows above 1.2000 indicate?
scenarios.explanation: Troughs printing higher above the 1.2000 base created ascending support compression into resistance.

scenarios.title: Psychological Round Number Support
scenarios.question: Why did price find strong institutional demand at exactly 1.1000?
scenarios.explanation: Major round figures (e.g. 1.1000) attract substantial institutional limit orders, serving as natural psychological support.

scenarios.title: Support Demand Absorption
scenarios.question: How is the absorption of heavy selling at 50.00 classified?
scenarios.explanation: Heavy selling pressure was absorbed completely at 50.00 without making a new low, leading to a strong bounce.

scenarios.title: Horizontal Resistance Ceiling
scenarios.question: Price repeatedly stalled at 1.0900 and dropped lower. What does 1.0900 represent?
scenarios.explanation: 1.0900 acted as a horizontal resistance ceiling where seller supply rejected price advances.

scenarios.title: Double Top Resistance Rejection
scenarios.question: What classic structural pattern was printed at 152.50?
scenarios.explanation: Two sequential peaks stalling at the same price ceiling (152.50) define a Double Top at resistance.

scenarios.title: Triple Resistance Test Ceiling
scenarios.question: What market behavior is demonstrated at 1.2800?
scenarios.explanation: Three distinct tests of 1.2800 failed to close higher, verifying a persistent resistance barrier.

scenarios.title: Shooting Star Pin Rejection at Resistance
scenarios.question: What did the long upper wick at 2052.0 in candle #2 communicate?
scenarios.explanation: A long upper wick touching 2052 and closing lower at 2036 shows strong seller rejection at resistance.

scenarios.title: Supply Resistance Zone
scenarios.question: How is the 1.1030–1.1050 area classified where buyers repeatedly stalled?
scenarios.explanation: A band of price where selling pressure consistently overcomes buying demand is a Resistance / Supply Zone.

scenarios.title: Resistance Compression (Ascending Triangle)
scenarios.question: What did shallow pullbacks forming Higher Lows into 1.0850 indicate?
scenarios.explanation: When sellers fail to push price deeply away from resistance, Higher Lows build pressure for an eventual breakout.

scenarios.title: Prior Swing High Acting as Resistance
scenarios.question: What structural reference capped the advance at candle #4?
scenarios.explanation: Previous major swing highs act as key resistance targets where sellers often re-enter.

options.text: Lower High Resistance capping the Downtrend

scenarios.explanation: In a downtrend, each pullback peak acts as a Lower High resistance ceiling.

scenarios.title: Range Box Resistance Boundary
scenarios.question: What is 50.00 in this horizontal consolidation box?
scenarios.explanation: 50.00 defines the upper boundary (resistance ceiling) of the horizontal range.

scenarios.title: Descending Resistance Pressure (Descending Triangle)
scenarios.question: What did Lower Highs pressing against support indicate?
scenarios.explanation: Sellers stepping in lower on each bounce created descending resistance pressure.

scenarios.title: Psychological Round Number Resistance
scenarios.question: Why did price sharply reject at exactly 1.2000?
scenarios.explanation: Major round figures (e.g. 1.2000) attract heavy sell orders, acting as psychological resistance.

scenarios.title: Bearish Engulfing at Resistance
scenarios.question: What confirmed the rejection at 100.0 in candle #3?
scenarios.explanation: A massive bearish body engulfing prior candles at 100.0 confirmed strong resistance rejection.

scenarios.title: Resistance Flips to Support (R → S Flip)
scenarios.question: 1.0850 was resistance in candle #1. What did it become in candle #4?
scenarios.explanation: Once broken, former resistance often flips to become support (polarity change).

scenarios.title: Support Flips to Resistance (S → R Flip)
scenarios.question: 1.2500 was support in candle #1. What did it become upon retest in candle #4?
scenarios.explanation: When a support floor breaks, it frequently flips to become a resistance ceiling on subsequent retests.

scenarios.title: Consolidation Box Flip
scenarios.question: How did the 2000.0 level behave after the breakout surge?

options.text: Flipped from Box Resistance into New Support Floor

scenarios.explanation: The prior 2000.0 ceiling converted into support, confirming the breakout and creating a new structural floor.

scenarios.title: Major Structural Level Polar Shift
scenarios.question: What term describes the transformation of 150.00 from resistance into support?
scenarios.explanation: When price breaks a major boundary and honors it from the opposite side, it is called a Polar Shift or Level Flip.

scenarios.title: Failed Resistance-to-Support Conversion
scenarios.question: What happened when the retest candle plunged through 100.0 to 97.5?
scenarios.explanation: Because the retest failed to hold above 100.0 and closed back below, the level flip failed.

scenarios.title: Channel Lower Band Flip
scenarios.question: How did 1.0800 function in candle #3 following the channel breakdown?
scenarios.explanation: The former channel support floor at 1.0800 acted as a resistance ceiling upon retest.

scenarios.title: Range Floor Broken and Retested as Resistance
scenarios.question: What structural principle is demonstrated when 50.00 rejects price in candle #4?

options.text: Broken Range Floor acting as New Resistance

scenarios.explanation: Breaking range support at 50.00 converts the former floor into a resistance ceiling on subsequent pullbacks.

scenarios.title: Multiple Retests Solidifying Flip Level
scenarios.question: What is confirmed by 1.1000 holding on two consecutive retest pullbacks?

options.text: Solidified New Support Base (Confirmed Polarity Flip)

scenarios.explanation: Multiple successful retest defenses solidify 1.1000 as a high-confidence support floor.
